body.name: bounded-relative-variation event-learner class
body.construction: For the fixed horizons in this note, the admissible event learners are those for which, conditionally on each training sample, \(R_{cf}(0\mid X)=0\), the relative-survival path \(R_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid X)\) is of bounded variation, and its total variation obeys the rate in Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-variation-rate}. A primitive sufficient certificate is available on the region where the survival ratio is defined: let \(e_{cf}(u\mid X)=\log\{Q_c(u\mid X)/\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid X)\}\). If \(e_{cf}(0\mid X)=0\), \(e_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid X)\) is c\`adl\`ag and of bounded variation, \(\max_{c,f}\|e_{cf}\|_\infty=o_P(1)\), and \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|\operatorname{TV}_{[0,t_{c\ell}]}(e_{cf})\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\), then \(R_{cf}=e^{e_{cf}}-1\) and the chain rule for bounded-variation paths gives \(V_{cf\ell}\le e^{\|e_{cf}\|_\infty}\operatorname{TV}_{[0,t_{c\ell}]}(e_{cf})\), which certifies the required variation rate. The \(0/0=1\) convention remains in force; outside this certificate, membership must be verified directly. This definition deliberately does not claim that ordinary survival-ratio \(L_2\) consistency implies the rate.
